newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Hyundai Petrochem union delays strike.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Hyundai Petrochem union delays strike.

text.p: Union workers at Hyundai Petrochemical Co, a unit of South Korea's Hyundai Group, postponed a strike planned for Thursday in protest at a new labour law, a union official said.
The union had planned to strike for one day on Thursday starting at 7:30 a.m. (2230 GMT Wednesday).

"We had a very low participation rate by union workers at a rally this morning and we've decided to delay the planned strike," the union official told Reuters. "Management have also worked hard to prevent the walkout."
He said the union would decide on Friday when to hold the strike.

"There is a strong possibility that we may join the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions' all-out strike on January 15," he said. The confederation called for general stoppages, including a public sector shutdown, on January 15 unless the government revoked the new labour law.
A strike would affect some 900 Hyundai union workers, he said. Hyundai Petrochemical has a total of 1,500 workers.

Strikes have crippled much of South Korean industry since the new labour law allowing layoffs, flexible work hours and the replacement of striking workers was rammed through parliament on December 26.
